title: Ram Kumar Gupta v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Ashwani Kumar Mishra, J.; Vipin Chandra Dixit, J.
disposition: Writ disposed of; petitioner permitted to approach the third respondent under Clause 6.5.
headnote: A grievance about load factor on an electricity connection and consequential billing is more appropriately examined by the concerned authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The petitioner was permitted to approach the third respondent, who shall consider the grievance and do the needful within four weeks.
facts: Ram Kumar Gupta filed Writ-C No. 4252 of 2025 in the Allahabad High Court against the State of Uttar Pradesh and three others. He complained of the load factor applied on his electricity connection and of the bills raised as a consequence. The short order does not set out any earlier forum decision, a quantified demand, or the identity of the distribution licensee beyond the array of respondents. Counsel for the petitioner was Virendra Singh Patel; the State and co-respondents were represented.

holding_units.holding: A grievance regarding load factor on an electricity connection and consequential billing can more appropriately be examined by the concerned authority under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The petitioner was permitted to approach the third respondent, who shall consider and examine that grievance and do the needful within four weeks. The writ petition was disposed of without a merits determination.

not_decided.point: Merits of the load-factor and consequential billing grievance
not_decided.note: Left to the third respondent under Clause 6.5; no finding on the connection or the bills.
